newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - FEB 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - FEB 11.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Investment euphoria saw in the week on the Athens bourse as the general price index broke through the "psychological barrier" of 1,200 points. The general price index rose 2.77 percent, to close at over 1,200 for the first time in six years. Sources say the reduced returns from state titles and deposit accounts - due to the continued fall of inflation and interest rates - has drawn foreign and domestic investment interest.

--The government and the Bank of Greece yesterday decided to change guidelines for the tender to sell state-run Cretabank. The national economy and finance ministry feels it is necessary to sell the bank and soon or risk damaging the credibility of the government's privatisation programme.

--The stock exchange has recorded impressive profits of over 30 percent since the beginning of the year, with banks and construction shares leading the rally. Some 33 shares noted a rise of 8.0 percent, closing at the limit up.
--The Greek state will finance the increase in OTE share capital with the aim of receiving revenues for the budget as well as allowing OTE to bring in capital to continue its investment programme.
--The escalating violence in Albania, as well as other Balkan countries, has Greek firms worried about continuing operations there.
--Some 427 firms and self-employed professionals will be charged with non-payment of Value Added Tax worth 1.2 billion drahcmas, following surprise checks by the finance ministry.

--The European Commission is reported to have recognised that Greece has met its convergence programme targets as regards the 1996 public deficit and, subseqeuntly, there is not risk of Cohesion Funds being cut off, at least for 1997.
--Greece will be able to take advantage of a transitional three-year period to prepare the Public Power Corporation (DEH) for the deregulated European market.
--Employees of the finance ministry's informatics department have threatened work stoppages for early next week if demands on their bonuses are not met by minister Yannos Papandoniou.
--Industrialists in Thrace said infrastructure works could turn around the situation in the region if they were completed promptly.
